$comment: Per-function `deno check` error ceilings for supabase/functions/**, enforced by
scripts/deno-check-functions.mjs and the `edge-typecheck` CI job.
EVERY CEILING IS NOW ZERO, and the ratchet's job has changed accordingly: it
is no longer paying down debt, it is keeping a clean tree clean. A new type
error in the edge tree fails the PR that introduces it.
A CEILING MAY ONLY BE LOWERED — which now means it may not be raised at all.
Raising one is never the right fix for a failing check: the change that added
the error is. There is no longer any such thing as an inherited edge type
error to hide behind.
The debt was not 83 individual mistakes. It was four places where type
checking had been switched off, and the errors were what leaked past them:
1. `createClient()` was called with no `Database` generic anywhere, so every
`.from()` row was `never` and every `.rpc()` argument was `undefined`.
Fixing it RAISED the count to 104 before removing it — real types see
real mismatches. `_shared/db-client.ts` now holds the one alias.
2. `.from<Row>('table')` — a supabase-js v1 idiom, 15 occurrences — silently
overrode the schema.
3. `validateQuery<T>(schema: z.ZodType<T>)` could bind `T` to a schema's
INPUT type, so every `.default()`ed field looked optional to handlers.
4. `createTracedClient().from()` defaulted its row to
`Record<string, unknown>`, and `single()`/`maybeSingle()` still typed the
result as an ARRAY — the origin of the `(org as { id: string }).id` cast
copied across eight org handlers.
Only one item was genuinely stale data: `blog_post_likes` (migration 00055)
was missing from `database.types.ts`. `database-types-freshness.spec.ts` now
compares migrations against the committed types, so the next omission is a red
test rather than a silent gap.
If this file ever needs a non-zero number again, that is a decision to write
down here with its reason — not a default.
